title: Logscan
summary: A log parser and summariser behind an on-call dashboard.

tasks.title: Truncated error messages
brief: The on-call dashboard’s “top errors” panel shows entries like “disk” and “could”. The raw logs say “disk full on /var” and “could not reach payments”, and different errors are being lumped together.
Find the cause and fix it. The dashboard team would like a test that pins the behaviour down.
done: Messages keep every word after the level.
top_messages groups by the whole message.
Lines without a message are still ignored.

questions: Should extra spaces inside a message be kept as they are? (Yes; only trim the ends.)
Is a line with a time and level but no message valid? (No, ignore it.)
orient: README shows the line format: time, level, then free text.
The symptom is in the dashboard, but top_messages only counts what parse_line gives it, so started at parse.py.
Baseline run: all green, because every test message is a single word.
walkthrough.failingTest:
def test_keeps_the_whole_message():
    assert parse_line("2026-03-04T09:30:00 ERROR disk full on /var")["message"] == "disk full on /var"  # fails: "disk"
trace: Printed parse_line(...) for the sample line: message was "disk".
line.split() splits on every space, and the code keeps only parts[2], the first word of the message.
split(" ", 2) splits at most twice, so the message keeps its spaces; the length check still rejects short lines.
wrapUp: Cause: the parser split the whole line on every space and kept only the first word of the message.
Fix: split at most twice, so the rest of the line is the message. One-line change plus a regression test.
Checked by hand: a missing message is still ignored, and lower-case levels still parse.
Noticed but not changed: tabs between fields are not supported; worth asking whether real logs use them.

tasks.title: Entries in a time window
brief: On-call engineers want to zoom in on an incident. Add between(lines, start, end) to logs/summary.py, returning parsed entries whose time is at or after start and before end, in log order.
Noise lines are skipped as usual. A window whose end is before its start is a caller mistake and should raise ValueError.
done: between returns entries with start <= time < end, in their original order.
An empty window returns []; a backwards window raises ValueError.

questions: Inclusive or exclusive ends? (Start inclusive, end exclusive, so back-to-back windows do not overlap.)
Strings or datetime objects? (The same ISO strings the logs use.)
Sorted by time or log order? (Log order.)
orient: summary.py already builds on parse_all, so the new function belongs beside count_by_level and top_messages.
Times share one fixed-width ISO format, so string comparison orders them correctly without parsing dates.
trace: parse_all drops noise and returns entries in order, so a single filter keeps log order for free.
wrapUp: Added between using the existing parse_all, with a guard for backwards windows.
Trade-off: comparing strings depends on every line using the same ISO format. Noted in the docstring.
With more time: accept datetime objects and time zones.
